title: Global idempotents and clopen subspaces of an algebraic space
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ with its small etale structure sheaf [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Give $|X|$ its atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology], and put $A=\Gamma(X_{\mathrm{et}},\mathcal O_X)$. There is a bijection $e\mapsto U_e$ between idempotents $e^2=e$ in $A$ and open subspaces of $X$ [def-a1-space-open-subspace] whose point images are closed. Their point images are exactly the clopen subsets of $|X|$, each with a unique open-subspace structure. For every affine etale chart $T=\operatorname{Spec}B\to X$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], the pullback of $U_e$ is the principal open $D(e|_T)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}B$. The inverse sends $U$ to the global section equal to $1$ on $U$ and $0$ on its complement. One has $U_0=\varnothing$, $U_1=X$, $U_{1-e}=X\setminus U_e$, and $U_{ef}=U_e\cap U_f$. No properness, quasi-compactness or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed; the empty space is allowed.

proof.text: Choose a representable surjective etale scheme atlas $p:P\to X$. Put $R=P\times_XP$, with projections $s,t$. The enlarged ringed-site model identifies $A$ with the equalizer of $\Gamma(P,\mathcal O_P)\rightrightarrows\Gamma(R,\mathcal O_R)$, naturally under etale base change. Thus restriction to $P$ is injective and ring operations are computed there. For $e^2=e$, write $a=e|_P$; then $a^2=a$ and $s^*a=t^*a$. Apply the scheme idempotent correspondence to obtain a clopen $V=U_a\subseteq|P|$. Its pullback compatibility gives $s^{-1}V=t^{-1}V$.

Put $C=|p|(V)$. The point fibre-product surjectivity says that any two points of $P$ with the same image in $X$ lift together to a point of $R$. The equality $s^{-1}V=t^{-1}V$ therefore gives $|p|^{-1}C=V$. Since $|p|$ is surjective and open, $C$ and its complement $|p|(|P|\setminus V)$ are open. The open-subspace classification gives a unique open subspace $U_e$ with image $C$. For any etale scheme chart $q:T\to X$, let $W=P\times_XT$ with projections $r:W\to P$ and $v:W\to T$. The atlas map $v$ is surjective, and $r^*a=v^*(e|_T)$. Scheme pullback compatibility gives $r^{-1}V=v^{-1}U_{e|_T}$. Point fibre-product surjectivity and $|p|^{-1}C=V$ identify the left side with $v^{-1}q^{-1}C$; surjectivity of $v$ gives $q^{-1}C=U_{e|_T}$. The open-subspace point calculus identifies this with the point image of $T\times_XU_e$. If $T=\operatorname{Spec}B$, the spectrum correspondence identifies $U_{e|_T}$ with $D(e|_T)$.

Conversely let $C\subseteq|X|$ be clopen, and let $U$ and $Z$ be the unique open subspaces for $C$ and its complement. By the point calculus their pullbacks to $P$ have point sets $V=|p|^{-1}C$ and $|P|\setminus V$. The scheme correspondence gives the unique idempotent $a$ equal to $1$ on $V$ and $0$ off $V$. On $R$, both $s^*a$ and $t^*a$ correspond to the same clopen $(ps)^{-1}C=(pt)^{-1}C$; scheme injectivity gives equality. The equalizer now descends $a$ to a unique $e\in A$. Since $a^2=a$, injectivity of restriction gives $e^2=e$. The chart formula in step 2 shows that its clopen is $C$. Moreover $e|_U=1$ and $e|_Z=0$: these equalities hold on the pulled-back scheme atlases, where they are exactly the defining restrictions of $a$, and are detected by the equalizer on $U$ and $Z$.

If two global idempotents give the same open subspace, their clopens on $P$ are equal by the chart formula. Scheme injectivity makes their restrictions equal, and equalizer injectivity makes the global sections equal. Together with step 3 this proves the claimed bijection and inverse. A section restricting to $1$ on $U$ and $0$ on $Z$ is unique even among all sections: on $P$ the two restrictions cover $P$ and the sheaf uniqueness axiom makes the sections equal; atlas injectivity then applies. Open-subspace uniqueness is exactly the existing open-subspace classification.

Finally $0,1,1-e,ef$ are idempotent by ring identities, using commutativity for $ef$. On $P$, idempotent germs are $0$ or $1$: the scheme correspondence says their nonzero locus is their one locus. Hence the loci for $0$ and $1$ are empty and full, the locus for $1-a$ is the complement of that for $a$, and the locus for $ab$ is the intersection of those for $a$ and $b$. The chart formula and surjectivity of $|p|$ give the same identities on $|X|$; uniqueness of open subspaces gives the asserted identities as subspaces. All arguments use arbitrary scheme atlases, with no finiteness assumptions. When $X$ is empty, the sheaf empty-cover axiom gives the zero ring of global sections; its sole idempotent corresponds to the sole open subspace, so all formulas still hold.

U : OpenSubspace X, pointImage U.val.ι = C) ∧ (∀ (e : {e : RingCat.sectionsSubring X.structurePresheaf // IsIdempotentElem e}) (B : CommRingCat.{u}) (p : Spec B ⟶ S) (a : yoneda.obj (Over.mk p) ⟶ X.obj.obj) (ha : IsEtale a), schemePointMap a ⁻¹' pointImage (E e).val.val.ι = (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso B).hom (e.val.val (op ⟨CostructuredArrow.mk a, ha⟩)))).carrier) ∧ (∀ (U : {U : OpenSubspace X // IsClosed (pointImage U.val.ι)}) (T : X.EtaleSite) (x : X.etaleForget.obj T), (schemePointMap T.obj.hom x ∈ pointImage U.val.val.ι → (X.etaleForget.obj T).presheaf.Γgerm x ((E.symm U).val.val (op T)) = 1) ∧ (schemePointMap T.obj.hom x ∉ pointImage U.val.val.ι → (X.etaleForget.obj T).presheaf.Γgerm x ((E.symm U).val.val (op T)) = 0)) ∧ (E 0).val.val = ⊥ ∧ (E 1).val.val = ⊤ ∧ (∀ e : {e : RingCat.sectionsSubring X.structurePresheaf // IsIdempotentElem e}, pointImage (E ⟨1 - e.val, e.property.one_sub⟩).val.val.ι = (pointImage (E e).val.val.ι)ᶜ) ∧ (∀ e f : {e : RingCat.sectionsSubring X.structurePresheaf // IsIdempotentElem e}, (E ⟨e.val * f.val, e.property.mul f.property⟩).val.val = (E e).val.val ⊓ (E f).val.val)
